searchText: We have no historic evidence of block producers being bad about the block size. Also, the rate of change is slow enough that we can see a problem coming enough in advance to address it with a soft fork. miners have the ability to increase the gas limit to from 12.5mm to 50mm in 10 minutes To me it's really about the strangeness of relying on block producers to be well intentioned, something that shouldn't be part of a blockchain. Not to mention that there is little upside to letting block producers have this power, especially when considering that the potential damage could be quite significant. I think your math is off here. I'm getting a bit under 6 hours. Could you explain how the max block size is set? I was under the impression that 12.5M was hardcoded into client validation logic. That being said, that is faster than I thought it would be. Similar magnitude 😛 Heh, I consider that a different order of magnitude, but I'm convinced it is a "dangerous" order still. Miners can set the gas limit to any number they want on a block they mine as long as it is within 1/1024 of the previous block's gas limit. So each block can change the gas limit by 1/1024th of the parent block. Interesting, so isn't there a greedy incentive to always make the next block 1/1024 bigger? Why isn't that happening today? There are certainly enough transactions in the mempool to fill larger blocks. If 100% of hashing power targets the same target, it can up to double or half every ~3 hours. The suspicion is a combination of: 1. Miners aren't all dicks like some people believe. 2. Miners know that if they behave against users, there will be a fork that takes away their power. (my math from above: `12.5 * (1 + 1/1024)^x = 50`, solving for x gives ~1420 which is about 6 hours of blocks) Ah yes, you’re right I was mistaken. I was thinking blocks could change by ~1% where it’s actually ~0.1%. Still, that means under 1559 in 6 hours there could be 100mm gas blocks 🙂 echoing this. one of the only security / network concerns i've seen related to 1559 is miners exploiting the block gas target as protest. While it's unlikely that miners would exploit this for short term benefits, if hardcoding it reduces uncertainty around 1559 guarantees, I'm all for it 😂 i think 1. is true, they seem to care about the network 😛 https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/798586271445680129/807252368365846548 Someone just paid $184.04 in gas to end a 1 year stake worth ~$14 million; <https://twitter.com/WhaleHex/status/1371465924516179969> and they paid $38.86 in gas to restake ~$10 million for 10 years in the HEX contract; <https://twitter.com/WhaleHex/status/1371567277456384002> Will 1559 make the network usable again for the little guy? Will Stable coins and other gas guzzlers finally move to layer 2?
